description: Hosted canary rollout workflow (GA) delivers a first-class Console workflow and underlying policy/routing controls to safely roll out changes on Hosted routes using percentage-based traffic splitting. The objective is to move existing/beta rollout primitives into a GA-ready experience: customers can define a rollout (baseline vs candidate model/version), set a percentage schedule (manual steps and optional timed progression), apply guardrails (error-rate/latency thresholds, max token cost deltas, and optional quality gates), and quickly pause/rollback. Scope spans: (1) Console UI + backend workflow (create/edit rollout, preview effective routing, audit history, rollback), (2) control-plane policy model + validation (entitlements, RBAC, safe defaults, deterministic evaluation), (3) data-plane routing integration for Hosted (weighted splits, sticky routing options, streaming/session behavior), (4) telemetry and monitoring (per-variant metrics, change events, canary comparison views), and (5) GA readiness (docs, release notes, support playbooks, SLOs, security audit logging). Key stakeholders: Product (Marissa Cole, Paula Mendes), Console & Tooling Eng (Dylan Brooks, Chloe Martin, Jada Williams), Platform Control Plane (Ethan Park, Benji Okafor, Jordan Lee), Smart Routing (Mina Haddad, Ravi Menon), Observability/Telemetry (Logan Wright, Nadia Rahman), SRE (Sean Gallagher, Allison Grant), and Security (Marcus Lin, Kevin Osei). Proposed timeline: Phase 0 discovery + PRD/design (2–3 weeks), Phase 1 implementation behind feature flag + internal dogfood (4–6 weeks), Phase 2 limited beta with select Hosted customers + hardening (3–5 weeks), Phase 3 GA launch with docs/support readiness and ongoing improvements (2–3 weeks). Constraints/risks include deterministic policy evaluation under high QPS, metric cardinality control for per-variant breakdowns, safe rollback semantics for streaming requests, and preventing misconfiguration (e.g., 100% candidate without guardrails) via validation and permissions.
